Had a bit of trouble getting the libraries setup on KiCAD nightly builds (AKA KiCAD 5).

After you install the nightly build you will need to download or clone the KiCAD 5 symbol, footprint and 3dpackages to the location of your choice. Eventually it looks like there will also be a templates repository as well but I didnt see it today. Git would be best as you are only downloading changes after the initial clone.

Once you have the libraries copy the /kicad-symbols-master/sym-lib-table and /kicad-footprints-master/fp-lib-table to your kicad .config folder. The location of your config folder will likely depend on your OS.

Then open KiCAD and select preferences/configure paths. Edit the location of your libraries. Symbol and templates is pretty self explanatory but for footprints use KISYSMOD and 3D packages use KISYS3DMOD. From there open PCBnew and set/verify the preferences/configure paths are set there as well.

Ima kicad rookie so anyone please correct me where I'm wrong. These are the steps it took for me. There is a kicad blog post here with info on testing the new kicad 5 libraries and getting your shit straight.

I also had a bit of trouble with the project specific footprint library, I'll show how I set mine up in a bit but first a little bit about how I currently understand the best practice to be concerning libraries and footprints. Master libraries for symbols, footprints, 3d models, etc... are held on github. When you want to update to the latest libraries you download or clone them from github to your location of choice and set your paths in kicad. The only problem with this is any custom symbols or footprints you build are overwritten when you update your libraries, or at least that is what I gather (There may be a way to update rather than overwrite but I dont know that yet). So for each project you should save all your custom symbols and footprints in a project specific symbol library and footprint library. To go even further, any symbol or footprint you pull from the downloaded github libraries should be saved as custom parts in your project specific libraries. This way if for any reason the part changes in the master libraries you wont have to worry if the changes will affect your design.

So, to add project specific libraries you need to take different steps for Eeschema and the Footprint Editor. In Eeschema you will add your library with the Symbol Library Editor. Click the Create new library icon and navigate to your project folder. Create a name for your library with extension .lib.

For your custom footprint library open the Footprint editor and click on the New footprint icon (1). Give your footprint a name and click the Create new library and save current footprint icon (2). The path base should be your project directory and just select OK. This will create a .pretty folder for your custom footprints. Now for me, I am running a Linux mint virtual machine with my project folder residing outside of the VM and accessible via shared folder settings in VirtualBox. Once you create your library you may need to add it to the paths for it to show up. Still in the footprint editor navigate to Preferences/Footprint library table and click the project specific libraries tab. Append a library and populate the library path. Once that is done you should be able to access the library as normal.

I should say that I am running the Linux Mint nightly builds. Putting this info out here for myself and anyone who also struggled a bit with getting these libraries setup. There is also a nice article on Hackaday though I believe it is for Kicad 4, which is the current stable version.
